correctness.rationale: Wiedmer proves PSO(A_Gamma'(Lambda)) is isomorphic to A_Lambda and finite index in Out(A_Gamma'(Lambda)), with quotient generated by vertex inversions and isomorphic to an elementary 2-group. If Out is acylindrically hyperbolic, its infinite finite-index normal PSO subgroup is s-normal, so Osin's theorem forces PSO to be acylindrically hyperbolic; the standard RAAG criterion gives the necessity. For edgeless Lambda, PSO=F_n is finite index, hence Out is virtually nonabelian free. I also rebuilt Gamma'(Lambda) independently with a plain adjacency implementation and reproduced the stated SIL counts and joined-outside property on the listed test graphs.
residual_risks: The record's informal phrase 'with inversion action' is not needed for parts (a)-(c); the audited conclusions rely only on the finite-index subgroup and quotient structure actually established by Wiedmer.
